summary: MarketProduct is a small, immutable data class that describes one item for sale at a farmers' market: its name, vendor, price, category, season, and whether it is organic. Later exercises in this chapter feed lists of these objects into streams for filtering, mapping, and grouping.

lines.text: This class exists only to hold data about one product, so it has no main method; it is compiled and then used by other classes.
The field is private so outside code cannot touch it directly, and final so it can never change after the object is built.
A price needs a decimal number, and double provides one. Production money code usually prefers BigDecimal, but double keeps the stream examples uncluttered.
A boolean is the right type for a yes-or-no fact, and it makes later filters such as "organic only" read naturally.

lines.text: The constructor takes every field as a parameter, so a MarketProduct is fully described the moment it is created.
The parameter and the field share a name, so this.name makes clear that the field is the target of the assignment.
A getter is the only way to read a private field from outside the class. Because the fields are final, there are no setters, which makes the object immutable.
By Java convention, a getter for a boolean is named with the prefix is rather than get, which is why this method is isOrganic instead of getOrganic.
This annotation tells the compiler that the method below is meant to replace one inherited from Object, so a typo in the signature becomes a compile error instead of a silent bug.
Without this method, printing a product would show a meaningless class name and hash code. Overriding it gives readable output whenever the object is printed or logged.
The value is assembled by joining string pieces with +, and the single quotes around the text fields make it obvious where each value starts and ends.
